name: Stone Hall

text: The Hall roll: every challenger since the Hall took the workings on,
in one long column, and a second column beside it headed DOWN and UP.
Everybody has an UP. Some of them took a week over theirs.
A chalked board by the shaft head.
TODAY'S DEPTH: SIXTY FATHOM. WATER: LOW. GAS: NONE.
The GAS line has been wiped and rewritten so often the slate has gone soft.
Eight Bond Crests in a glass case, one for every Hall in Caelora.
The Quarry Crest sits second from the left, and is the plainest thing there.
The case is dusty. Somebody polishes the brass outside instead.
A cutaway model of the workings, six galleries deep.
Three of them are hatched over in red pencil.
The label under the red says only: WATER.
The counterweight gear, dressed and greased and going nowhere.
A rope comes off it and disappears into the floor.
Whatever is on the other end of that rope is not in this room.
A photograph, faded: a shift of forty on the west face, hats off.
Second from the left, arms folded, refusing to smile at the camera,
is a much younger woman with exactly the same expression she has now.
A fern in a pot, thriving, at the top of a mine shaft.
Somebody has been carrying it out to the light and back every day
for what the leaf count suggests is about eleven years.

_plan: The Hall is a waiting room and a shaft head, not an arena. Roxen keeps her Hall the way she kept the west face -- at the bottom of it -- so the challenge is the old workings and the Keeper is at the far end of them. The man-engine ladder at 4,3 is the way back up once she is beaten; it only opens from below, which is why nobody walks in the front door and straight down to her.
